purpose: Optional human-language augmentation layered above raw governed entities.

SAGE-ACTION-20260815-002.what_this_means: SAGE learned how to move build outputs toward deployment while preserving exactly which artifact was produced and avoiding a hidden rebuild during promotion.
SAGE-ACTION-20260815-002.what_it_enables: A future delivery path can start with stronger artifact identity, provenance, portability, and promotion expectations instead of rediscovering those requirements from scratch.
SAGE-ACTION-20260815-002.why_it_matters: Without this, a release can quietly depend on a particular machine or produce a different artifact later than the one that was reviewed.
SAGE-ACTION-20260815-002.historical_effort_context: The original path included discovery and remediation work needed to establish reusable controls. That historical iteration is evidence about the cost of discovering comparable new complexity, not a prediction that the same remediated work must recur.
SAGE-ACTION-20260815-002.reusable_value_created: Portable-stage, artifact-promotion, provenance, and engine-neutral orchestration experience became available as a stronger starting point for later delivery objectives.
SAGE-ACTION-20260815-002.expected_repeat_effect: Comparable future delivery work should avoid some one-time discovery and remediation costs when the same reusable constraints apply, but genuinely new environment or integration complexity still requires fresh evidence.
limits: Historical experience does not prove current runtime readiness.
Transfer to a new environment remains contextual and requires revalidation.
